SUBJECT: the COURTHOUSE, the town's seat of law and its biggest building, a grand civic Tudor hall FIVE tiles wide. Its landmark is a tall square CLOCK TOWER rising from the centre of the roof, with a big round clock face (a plain white dial with black hands, no numerals) under a small white-roofed cap and a spire. A wide front of two storeys with rows of leaded windows, a grand double door at the top of a short flight of broad stone steps, two stone pillars or a small porch roof framing the door, a balcony or a row of flags is welcome. ACCENT: deep burgundy wine-red on the double door and the shutters only, and a gold rim on the clock face; the roof stays white, the walls cream. SIGN: NONE, no placard: the clock tower is the sign. PROPS: a stone lantern or two flanking the steps, nothing else. LOOK: town: clean, no moss, no vines. It must read as the courthouse / town hall at a glance, stately and symmetric. The LAST attached image is a layout guide, a patch of the board grid with a tan 5 x 5 square: the building's walls and ground contact fill that 5 x 5 square almost to its edges, end to end (the roof, the clock tower and its spire may rise above it), with a soft contact shadow. Fill the surrounding squares with plain short grass in the same style, no props beyond those named, and draw the faint grid lines as thin tile edges. Do not leave the tan square tan.
